spec.title: MCP-CORE v0.1 — the neutral MCP server transport

p.fact: **Status:** SHIPPED with discipline-core 0.6.0 (MCP-SOVEREIGNTY-PLAN Wave 2); the flow foundation is named core-ai-native since the package-family rename (PROP-028), and the crate ships as core-ai-native-mcp.
The transport every `mcp`-kind package's server builds on: this package owns what no single language owns, and a JSON-RPC loop is exactly that.
Consumers: the per-language discipline servers (`rust-ai-native-mcp`, `typescript-ai-native-mcp`) vendor this crate byte-identically (sync-engines) and mount their tool sets on it.

**Related:** the consumer-side kind and delivery laws live in the consuming repo's PROP-027 (`spec://org.vibevm.core/vibevm/modules/vibe-mcp/PROP-027`); the tcg tool grammar in TCG-PROTOCOL-RUST-v0.1 / TCG-PROTOCOL-v0.1 (the stacks) is transport-independent and unchanged by this mechanism.
`req r1`

Line-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio — one JSON object per line, no Content-Length framing (that is the LSP convention; MCP hosts speak lines, and the production vibe-mcp server has spoken exactly this shape against every supported agent host since PROP-015).
The answered protocol revision is `2024-11-05`.
Inbound frames classify by `id`:

item.fact: present-and-non-null = a REQUEST that MUST be answered;
absent-or-null = a NOTIFICATION that MUST be absorbed without a response (hosts send `notifications/initialized` and cancellations).

p.fact: A malformed line — non-JSON, or a frame without `method` — is answered with JSON-RPC `parse error` (-32700) and MUST NOT kill the loop: the loop ends only at end-of-input or a dead channel.
Transport-level failure is the layer's one `thiserror` enum, each variant citing this mechanism and naming a fix surface.
`req r1`

The server is `(name, version, ToolSet)` driven over a `Transport` seam (`read_line` / `write_line`; production = locked stdio, tests = a scripted replay double — the whole loop tests with no agent host near the suite).
Methods:

item.fact: `tools/call` → dispatch by `name` with `arguments`; a missing `name` is `invalid params` (-32602); an unknown tool is `method not found` (-32601).

p.fact: `req r1`
A tool is `descriptor()` (name, description, `inputSchema` JSON schema) plus `run(args) → ToolOutput{report, is_error}`.
The registry maps name → tool; the last registration of a name wins.

**Tool-level failure is a RESULT, never a protocol error**: a gate that found findings, an oracle that refused — these answer `{content:[{type:"text",text:report}], isError:true}` so the agent reads the report; protocol errors are reserved for the transport grammar itself (unknown tool, malformed params).
Reports speak the Class-F REQ-citing grammar of the runners they wrap.
`req r1`

Everything a tool run says — including CHILD processes (a floor's cargo, prettier, node) — goes to the process's stderr channel, so the only capture that sees a whole run is a process-level redirect around the call: `dup2` over fd 2 on unix, `SetStdHandle(STD_ERROR_HANDLE, …)` on Windows, into a temp FILE (a file, not a pipe — a filling pipe blocks the writer and deadlocks a chatty floor).
A threaded `&mut dyn Write` was rejected at the plan's Wave-0 spike: children inherit the process handle and bypass it entirely.

Laws: the redirect is process-global, so captures MUST NOT nest or run concurrently (the loop dispatches tools sequentially — that is the licence); a second simultaneous capture refuses with this unit cited.
Restoration rides `Drop`, so a panicking tool cannot leave the process mute.
This cell is the crate's audited home of raw-descriptor unsafety — nothing else touches fds or std handles.
`req r1`
A server has no interactive channel: tools MUST NOT prompt — anything that would ask becomes an explicit tool parameter (`force`-class flags included).

And nothing in this crate knows vibe, a language, or a discipline rule: a server built on it serves with `vibe` absent from `PATH` — the consuming repo's PROP-027 §2.6 turns that property into an acceptance test.
